title: Choose K Elements With Maximum Sum
summary: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length n, and a positive integer k, for each index i in nums1, identify indices j where nums1[j] is less than nums1[i].
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length n, and a positive integer k, for each index i in nums1, identify indices j where nums1[j] is less than nums1[i]. Select at most k values from nums2[j] to maximize the sum. The result is an array answer where answer[i] is the sum for index i.
constraints: nums1 and nums2 have equal nonzero length and k is positive.
For each i, only indices j with nums1[j] strictly less than nums1[i] are eligible.
Return the maximum sum of at most k eligible nums2 values for every i.
hints: Sorting indices by nums1 lets each query reuse all previously activated strictly smaller keys.
Sweep equal-value groups while a min-heap retains the k largest activated nums2 values.
Before answering a key, add only earlier groups with smaller keys; update the heap sum and write it to every original index in the group.
The heap exactly represents the optimal top-k eligible values, and delaying equal keys enforces strictness.
editorial: The heap exactly represents the optimal top-k eligible values, and delaying equal keys enforces strictness.

tests.explanation: Equal nums1 values are not strictly smaller, so both answers are zero.
